string-array.name: help_subscriptions
string-array.item: Purpose: Manage groups and remote subscriptions without changing unrelated saved profiles.
Before you start: Treat subscription URLs as secrets and verify who maintains each feed.
How to use: Select a group, import or refresh it, then inspect the displayed count.
How to interpret: A rejected empty or malformed update must preserve the previous valid profiles; a failed test is not permanent invalidity.
Risks and recovery: Keep a private backup before replacing a feed; inspect the source and connection when refresh fails.

string-array.name: help_settings
string-array.item: Purpose: Configure VPN or proxy mode, DNS, routing, ports and testing preferences.
Before you start: Some changes take effect only after service restart; review the active connection first.
How to use: Change one option at a time and verify the actual route instead of just direct DNS or TCP.
How to interpret: Keep TLS certificate checks on by default. The insecure option is an explicit exception; custom JSON may define its own TLS policy.
Risks and recovery: Restore recent changes if connectivity breaks; remove credentials before sharing logs.

string-array.name: help_assets
string-array.item: Purpose: Manage GeoIP and Geosite files used by routing rules.
Before you start: Use trusted sources and keep a known-good version of each required file.
How to use: Import an asset and reload or restart the relevant routing state as needed.
How to interpret: A file being present does not prove the VPN is connected or correctly routed.
Risks and recovery: A corrupt or outdated file can misroute traffic; restore a known-good asset.

string-array.name: help_logs
string-array.item: Purpose: Read app and native-core diagnostic messages for connection failures.
Before you start: Record the app version, approximate failure time and chosen test method.
How to use: Copy only relevant lines and remove sensitive data before requesting support.
How to interpret: DNS, TCP, core-start and tunneled HTTP errors describe different failures.
Risks and recovery: Logs can expose subscription URLs, passwords, tokens, IPs and private keys.

string-array.name: help_import
string-array.item: Purpose: Add profiles by QR, clipboard, file, URL or manual entry.
Before you start: An imported profile can contain secrets and untrusted routing or transport details.
How to use: Check endpoint, protocol, SNI, TLS and transport before connecting.
How to interpret: Saving a profile does not prove connectivity; choose a suitable TCP or through-proxy test.
Risks and recovery: Never post raw profile links publicly; preserve existing working profiles after a bad import.

string-array.name: help_filter
string-array.item: Purpose: Show only a chosen group or search result without deleting other profiles.
Before you start: Hidden groups still exist and may retain previous delay observations.
How to use: Select a group or filter, then act only on the visible targets.
How to interpret: Zero delay means no accepted measurement, not a failed or invalid server.
Risks and recovery: Clear the filter to see all profiles before broad operations.

string-array.name: help_restart
string-array.item: Purpose: Restart the current VPN or proxy service to apply supported settings.
Before you start: Traffic is interrupted during restart and VPN permission may be requested.
How to use: Verify the selected profile and mode before restarting.
How to interpret: A running native core alone does not prove an HTTP request succeeds through the tunnel.
Risks and recovery: If restart fails, review service cleanup errors and try again after it finishes.

string-array.name: help_delete_all
string-array.item: Purpose: Remove all locally saved configurations; this is not a connectivity test.
Before you start: This action is destructive and has no built-in recycle bin.
How to use: Export a private backup, read the confirmation, then delete only if intended.
How to interpret: Clearing saved selection does not necessarily stop the currently loaded tunnel immediately.
Risks and recovery: Backups may contain passwords and access tokens; store them privately.

string-array.name: help_delete_duplicates
string-array.item: Purpose: Remove duplicate profiles in the displayed scope after confirming the candidate count.
Before you start: Hidden groups and the selected profile must not be affected.
How to use: Check your filter and the preview count before confirming.
How to interpret: Similar display names can represent different accounts or transport settings.
Risks and recovery: Removal is irreversible; export a private backup when needed.

string-array.name: help_delete_failed
string-array.item: Purpose: Review and manually remove profiles with accepted negative test evidence in the displayed scope.
Before you start: Zero means untested; cancelled, unknown, stale, unsupported and hidden results are not eligible failure evidence.
How to use: Run a compatible test, review the scope and candidate count, and explicitly confirm.
How to interpret: A TCP failure cannot prove a UDP or QUIC route invalid; a transient outage can produce negative results.
Risks and recovery: Deleting stored profiles is irreversible; keep private backups and do not rely on old results.

string-array.name: help_export
string-array.item: Purpose: Export non-custom profile entries to the clipboard for backup or transfer.
Before you start: Exported configurations may include passwords and subscription credentials.
How to use: Paste only into a secure destination and verify the backup before deleting originals.
How to interpret: Custom JSON profiles may require a separate backup; an export is not a connectivity check.
Risks and recovery: Clear the clipboard afterward and never publish configuration text in a public issue.

string-array.name: help_tcp
string-array.item: Purpose: Measure TCP socket reachability to a target host and port.
Before you start: This test does not establish UDP, QUIC, TLS identity or complete proxy function.
How to use: Choose a visible group and an appropriate supported timeout and concurrency policy.
How to interpret: Positive means TCP connected; zero means untested; negative means that attempt failed.
Risks and recovery: Large parallel batches consume data and can trigger rate limits or transient failures.

string-array.name: help_real_ping
string-array.item: Purpose: Run the supported native proxy request rather than a direct DNS or TCP probe.
Before you start: The native core and target network must be ready for this method.
How to use: Choose visible profiles, start the batch, and allow completion or cancel intentionally.
How to interpret: A positive result proves only the measured route and request at that moment; stale or cancelled results do not prove failure.
Risks and recovery: Long batches use battery and data; network changes and native delays can leave results unknown.

string-array.name: help_sort
string-array.item: Purpose: Reorder saved profiles by comparable test observations without deleting them.
Before you start: Identify the method, scope and age of the result before comparing values.
How to use: Test appropriate targets when needed, then sort the current profile list.
How to interpret: Unknown and untested entries are not failures and historical values may be stale.
Risks and recovery: Sorting changes order only; reconnect or retest after changing networks.

string-array.name: help_refresh
string-array.item: Purpose: Refresh enabled subscription groups from their remote sources.
Before you start: Verify source trust and protect subscription URLs containing credentials.
How to use: Refresh selected groups, then review the imported count and currently selected profile.
How to interpret: Empty or malformed feeds should retain known-good profiles; partial changes require review.
Risks and recovery: Remote updates may change credentials and routing, so keep private backups and verify account identity.
